title: Fix Android icon-tap DOMException crash and localize crash UI to English

requirements.summary: Prevent Android Chrome DOMException (removeChild) crash triggered by tapping icon-based controls (bottom tabs and header icon buttons).
acceptanceCriteria: On Android Chrome, tapping each bottom navigation tab (Dashboard, Calendar, Journal, Reports) no longer triggers the ErrorBoundary and does not freeze the UI.
On Android Chrome, tapping header icon/buttons (e.g., login/logout button with icon) no longer triggers the ErrorBoundary.
No DOMException removeChild error is emitted in the browser console during these interactions.

file_operations.description: Harden tab button interactions for Android: ensure the click/tap target is always the button (disable pointer events on nested icon elements), add touch-action optimizations, and avoid event sequences that can trigger DOM removeChild issues during re-renders.

Harden header icon-button interactions (login/logout and any other icon-bearing controls) to avoid Android tap-related DOM removeChild crashes by stabilizing event handling and ensuring nested icons are not separate pointer targets.
Stabilize the dialog trigger button interaction on mobile (icon + label) to prevent tap-driven DOM removeChild crashes when Radix/shadcn dialog portals mount/unmount during user interaction.

Add or adjust shared CSS utility classes for icon buttons (e.g., touch-action manipulation and safe pointer targeting) and apply them via existing className composition to reduce Android Chrome tap/ghost-click edge cases.
Ensure tab switching state updates are safe and consistent during rapid taps (no extra navigation features); keep rendering stable during tab changes to avoid DOM removeChild issues on Android.

requirements.summary: Add a small Android regression checklist and console-only debug logging for tab switches and icon-button taps without adding user-visible UI.
acceptanceCriteria: A developer can reproduce/verify the fix using a short documented checklist (e.g., steps to tap each icon-based control).
Console logs (only) clearly indicate which control was tapped and which tab was requested, without logging sensitive user data.
No additional debug UI is visible to end users in production screens.

file_operations.description: Document a short, explicit regression checklist for Android Chrome focused on tapping bottom tabs and header icon-buttons, and verifying no ErrorBoundary/DOMException occurs.
Add a small console-only debug logger (gated by dev mode and/or an opt-in localStorage flag) to log UI control taps and requested tab changes without logging any sensitive user data.
Integrate console-only debug logging for each bottom nav icon-tab tap (log tab id/label only) using the new debug logging helper.
Integrate console-only debug logging for header icon-button taps (e.g., login/logout) using the new debug logging helper; ensure no user data is included.
Log tab-change requests (requested tab id only) using the debug logging helper; keep logs console-only with no UI changes.

requirements.summary: Localize the global ErrorBoundary crash screen user-facing text to English while keeping technical error details visible and recovery actions working.
acceptanceCriteria: When the ErrorBoundary is shown, the title/description/buttons are in English (e.g., "Something went wrong", "Reload app", "Go back").
The technical error message text (e.g., the DOMException message) remains visible in the details section as it is today.
The ErrorBoundary remains recoverable via reload and back actions.

file_operations.description: Replace the ErrorBoundary title/description/button labels with English copy while keeping the underlying error.message detail section unchanged and preserving reload/back recoverability.
